name: Jissjia
title: A descendant of Harim who sent away his foreign wife
summary: Jissjia was one of the Israelites who had taken a foreign wife after the exile. He is mentioned among those who, during Ezra's time, committed themselves to sending away their foreign wives to restore purity in the people. His action was part of the great reform movement led by Ezra to preserve Israel's spiritual identity.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among those who had taken foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jissjia is listed among the sons of Harim who had married foreign women in violation of God's law.

keyEvents.title: Commitment to send away foreign wives
keyEvents.description: The people, including Jissjia, committed themselves to sending away their foreign wives and their children as part of Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's prayer and confession for the people
keyEvents.description: Ezra prayed and confessed the people's sin of taking foreign wives, which concerned Jissjia and the other named men.

keyEvents.title: The assembly in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: All the men of Judah and Benjamin were gathered in Jerusalem to address the matter of the foreign wives, where Jissjia was among those affected.
